lede: A hotter October core CPI has a December Fed hike close to fully priced, lifting the dollar index to its highest since April 2025 and pushing gold back below $4,000. Wall Street gained 1.3% on CoreWeave's results, but Nasdaq futures slipped overnight after a report that Nvidia's board may replace CEO Jensen Huang.
snapshot_time: Gold & Brent ≈06:30 TRT · FX & US500 = Wed close

focus.text: Hot core CPI, a 5% 10-year yield and a firmer dollar pushed gold under $4,000; near 3,978, below the 4,011 pivot. Today: US jobless claims and six Fed speakers.
Slid 0.67% to about 1.1089, a two-week low, as Fed hike bets outweighed a hawkish ECB tone. Today's risks: Lagarde and Nagel remarks, then US claims at 16:30.

ECB's Lagarde, Nagel and Vujčić speak; ECB Economic Bulletin

news.text: Core CPI's 0.3% rise left markets pricing roughly 87–90% odds of a December hike; Waller had flagged a 50bp move at that reading.
The dollar index touched about 102.96, its strongest since April 2025, while the 10-year Treasury yield hovered near 5%.
S&P 500 rose 1.3% to 7,619 as CoreWeave jumped 25%; Nvidia then fell about 8% after hours on a WSJ report about its CEO.
Brent eased about 1% toward $92 after Saudi output rose sharply in October and API reported a 9m-barrel US crude build; US–Iran talks remain stuck.
Gold closed below $4,000 again; Goldman attributes most recent selling to momentum funds, while central banks bought 321 tonnes in Q3.
US spot bitcoin ETFs saw about $95m of net outflows on 10 Nov, a fourth straight losing day, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for $78m.
MSCI will drop bitcoin-treasury firms including Strategy and Metaplanet after 30 Nov; Strategy estimates up to ~$2.8bn of passive selling of its shares.
Deutsche Bank opened a digital-asset custody service for initial clients, covering BTC, ETH and USDC.
The CPI whipsaw triggered roughly $725m of crypto liquidations, mostly longs; ether liquidations exceeded bitcoin's. Fear & Greed sits in 'fear' near 26–28.
Zcash dropped about 13% as longs were flushed and its Grayscale ETF saw outflows; PEPE lost about 16% in 24 hours, while Hyperliquid's HYPE won Korean won listings.
Glassnode data show stablecoin supply shrank about $14.2bn in 30 days, the steepest drop since 2022, a sign of thinner buying power.
